item.title: Raptor Migration at its Best — Fri Oct 9, 8:00 AM — NJ
item.description: Join CMBO Director Brett Ewald and CMBO Naturalists for this workshop. Bird the “raptor capital of North America” at the peak of diversity. Bird the “raptor capital of North America” at the peak of diversity, when falcons are zipping along the dunes, accipiters are flap, flap, flapping by, buteos are soaring overhead, and eagles are chasing Ospreys. Early October often produces flights in the thousands and is the peak time for Peregrine Falcons and others. It is a rare moment during October in Cape May when raptors are not in view and this concentration of birds should ensure that we almost always have something to look at. Learn how to tell buteos from accipiters, falcons from eagles, at the very edge of your eyesight or right overhead, and focus on tricky species-pairs, such as the many ways to tell Sharp-shinned from Cooper’s Hawks. We’ll visit areas around Cape May to make the most of your raptor watching on this “in the field” workshop. We’ll also be in a prime location to enjoy o

item.title: Author Visit with Melinda Gonzalez for Latin American Heritage Month — Sat Oct 10, 12:00 PM — Montclair Main - Green Room
item.description:
Join us on Saturday October 10th at 12pm for a celebration for culture community and neurodiversity As Dr. Melinda Gonzalez visits and reads her childrens book: Curious Mind and Dancing Feet.
Dr. Melinda González is a Puerto Rican scholar and poet, who was born and raised in Newark, New Jersey, with ancestral home in the lush mountains of Moca, Puerto Rico. She is a socio-cultural anthropologist who focuses on environmental anthropology/disaster studies.
In her book Curious Mind and Dancing Feet, we meet a young Puerto Rican Muslim girl with ADHD. She explains what life is like from her perspective; vibrant, exciting, colorful, and sometimes overwhelming.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

item.title: Tech Toolbox: Setting Up Emergency Info — Tue Oct 27, 12:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Toolbox is a free hands-on workshop series focused on building real, practical digital skills. Each session zeroes in on a specific skill, program, or tool—from core computer skills and file management to navigating software and online platforms you use every day. Participants are encouraged to bring their own devices and follow along, so you'll leave each session having actually practiced what you learned.
All experience levels are welcome, and your instructor will be there to walk you through everything step by step. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: Setting Up Emergency Info
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Tech Talks: Staying Safe While Traveling — Tue Oct 27, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: Staying Safe While Traveling
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: An Autumn Sicilian Dinner: Cooking Demo and Tasting NEW — Tue Oct 27, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
Celebrate Italian Heritage and Culture Month with an Autumn Sicilian Dinner.
Join Donna Liotto-Scocozza of Firenze International Olive Oils for an Italian-inspired menu filled with bold flavors, comforting classics and a touch of nostalgia. The menu includes a colorful Sicilian Olive Salad; Chicken and Sausage Cacciatore, a rustic braise with tomatoes, peppers and herbs, served over crispy-outside, creamy-inside PanGrilled Polenta. Chocolate-Swirl Biscuit Tortoni, a cool, creamy Italian-American favorite will complete the menu. Along the way, Donna will talk about ingredients, techniques, and simple ways to bring the generous spirit of the Italian table into your own kitchen.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series — Mon Nov 2, 5:30 PM — Cole Hall 141
item.description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14. This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. item.description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/225105
What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town.
Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. item.description:

Cooking authentic Korean food at home doesn't have to be intimidating or complicated—in fact, it can be as fun and engaging as reading your favorite graphic novel! Join us for a virtual conversation with artist and author Robin Ha as we explore her New York Times bestselling book, Cook Korean!: A Comic Book Cookbook.
Fun to look at and easy to use, this unique combination of cookbook and graphic novel is the ideal introduction to cooking Korean cuisine at home.
